# zunbdb3

> Simultaneously bidiagonalizes the blocks of a tall and skinny complex matrix `[X11; X21]` with orthonormal columns (variant 3 — `M-P` is the minimum dimension).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zunbdb3 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zunbdb3';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zunbdb3(
    order,
    M, P, Q,
    X11, LDX11,
    X21, LDX21,
    THETA, strideTHETA,
    PHI, stridePHI,
    TAUP1, strideTAUP1,
    TAUP2, strideTAUP2,
    TAUQ1, strideTAUQ1,
    WORK
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Total number of rows<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `P` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows in `X11`<br>Rejects `2 * P < M \|\| P > M` |
| `Q` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Rejects `Q < M - P \|\| M - Q < M - P` |
| `X11` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>P × Q</sub> | **in/out** · Top block (`P`-by-`Q`) |
| ↳ `LDX11` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `X11`<br>Column-major requires `LDX11 ≥ max(1, P)`<br>Row-major requires `LDX11 ≥ max(1, Q)` |
| `X21` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(M - P) × Q</sub> | **in/out** · Bottom block (`(M-P)`-by-`Q`) |
| ↳ `LDX21` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `X21`<br>Column-major requires `LDX21 ≥ max(1, M - P)`<br>Row-major requires `LDX21 ≥ max(1, Q)` |
| `THETA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length Q</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `Q`) |
| ↳ `strideTHETA` | `integer` | Stride length for `THETA` |
| `PHI` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length Q - 1</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `Q-1`) |
| ↳ `stridePHI` | `integer` | Stride length for `PHI` |
| `TAUP1` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length P</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `P`) |
| ↳ `strideTAUP1` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAUP1` (in complex elements) |
| `TAUP2` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length M - P</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `M-P`) |
| ↳ `strideTAUP2` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAUP2` (in complex elements) |
| `TAUQ1` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length Q</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `Q`) |
| ↳ `strideTAUQ1` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAUQ1` (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(2 + max(max(P, M - P - 1), Q - 1) - 1, 2 + (Q - 1) - 1)</sub> | **out** · Workspace (length at least the reference LWORKMIN `max(P, M-P-1, Q-1) + 1` complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows `X11` plus the number of rows in `X21`.
- `P`: The number of rows in `X11`. $0 \le P \le M$. $M-P \le \min (P,Q,M-Q)$.
- `Q`: The number of columns in `X11` and `X21`. $0 \le Q \le M$.
- `X11`: On entry, the top block of the matrix X to be reduced. On exit, the columns of tril(`X11`) specify reflectors for P1 and the rows of triu(`X11`,1) specify reflectors for Q1.
- `X21`: On entry, the bottom block of the matrix X to be reduced. On exit, the columns of tril(`X21`) specify reflectors for P2.
- `THETA`: The entries of the bidiagonal blocks B11, B21 are defined by `THETA` and `PHI`. See Further Details.
- `PHI`: The entries of the bidiagonal blocks B11, B21 are defined by `THETA` and `PHI`. See Further Details.
- `TAUP1`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors that define P1.
- `TAUP2`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors that define P2.
- `TAUQ1`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors that define Q1.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `info` (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `2 * P < M \|\| P > M`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `Q < M - P \|\| M - Q < M - P`)
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, P )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, Q )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M - P )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, Q )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` `M` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `P` must satisfy `2*P >= M && P <= M`
- `RangeError` `Q` must satisfy `Q >= M-P && M-Q >= M-P`
- `RangeError` `LDX11` must satisfy the leading-dimension constraint
- `RangeError` `LDX21` must satisfy the leading-dimension constraint

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zunbdb3.ndarray(
    M, P, Q,
    X11, strideX111, strideX112, offsetX11,
    X21, strideX211, strideX212, offsetX21,
    THETA, strideTHETA, offsetTHETA,
    PHI, stridePHI, offsetPHI,
    TAUP1, strideTAUP1, offsetTAUP1,
    TAUP2, strideTAUP2, offsetTAUP2,
    TAUQ1, strideTAUQ1, offsetTAUQ1,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Total number of rows<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `P` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows in `X11`<br>Rejects `2 * P < M \|\| P > M` |
| `Q` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Rejects `Q < M - P \|\| M - Q < M - P` |
| `X11` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>P × Q</sub> | **in/out** · Top block (`P`-by-`Q`) |
| ↳ `strideX111` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `X11` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideX112` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `X11` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX11` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `X11` (in complex elements) |
| `X21` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(M - P) × Q</sub> | **in/out** · Bottom block (`(M-P)`-by-`Q`) |
| ↳ `strideX211` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `X21` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideX212` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `X21` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX21` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `X21` (in complex elements) |
| `THETA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length Q</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `Q`) |
| ↳ `strideTHETA` | `integer` | Stride length for `THETA` |
| ↳ `offsetTHETA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `THETA` |
| `PHI` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length Q - 1</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `Q-1`) |
| ↳ `stridePHI` | `integer` | Stride length for `PHI` |
| ↳ `offsetPHI` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `PHI` |
| `TAUP1` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length P</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `P`) |
| ↳ `strideTAUP1` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAUP1` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetTAUP1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `TAUP1` (in complex elements) |
| `TAUP2` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length M - P</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `M-P`) |
| ↳ `strideTAUP2` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAUP2` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetTAUP2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `TAUP2` (in complex elements) |
| `TAUQ1` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length Q</sub> | **out** · Output array (length at least `Q`) |
| ↳ `strideTAUQ1` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAUQ1` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetTAUQ1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `TAUQ1` (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(2 + max(max(P, M - P - 1), Q - 1) - 1, 2 + (Q - 1) - 1)</sub> | **out** · Workspace (length at least the reference LWORKMIN `max(P, M-P-1, Q-1) + 1` complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows `X11` plus the number of rows in `X21`.
- `P`: The number of rows in `X11`. $0 \le P \le M$. $M-P \le \min (P,Q,M-Q)$.
- `Q`: The number of columns in `X11` and `X21`. $0 \le Q \le M$.
- `X11`: On entry, the top block of the matrix X to be reduced. On exit, the columns of tril(`X11`) specify reflectors for P1 and the rows of triu(`X11`,1) specify reflectors for Q1.
- `X21`: On entry, the bottom block of the matrix X to be reduced. On exit, the columns of tril(`X21`) specify reflectors for P2.
- `THETA`: The entries of the bidiagonal blocks B11, B21 are defined by `THETA` and `PHI`. See Further Details.
- `PHI`: The entries of the bidiagonal blocks B11, B21 are defined by `THETA` and `PHI`. See Further Details.
- `TAUP1`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors that define P1.
- `TAUP2`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors that define P2.
- `TAUQ1`: The scalar factors of the elementary reflectors that define Q1.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `info` (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `2 * P < M \|\| P > M`)
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `Q < M - P \|\| M - Q < M - P`)
- `RangeError` `M` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `P` must satisfy `2*P >= M && P <= M`
- `RangeError` `Q` must satisfy `Q >= M-P && M-Q >= M-P`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit.
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zunbdb3()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZUNBDB3`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zunbdb3.f).
-   The bidiagonal blocks `B11`, `B21` are represented implicitly by the angles `THETA(1..M-P)` and `PHI(1..M-P-1)`. Every entry of the bidiagonal band is a product of a sine or cosine of a `THETA` with a sine or cosine of a `PHI`.
-   `P1`, `P2`, `Q1` are unitary matrices represented as products of Householder reflectors. See `zuncsd2by1` for details on generating them via `zungqr` and `zunglq`.
-   The diagonal entries of `X11` and `X21` after reduction are real-and-non-negative (a property of `zlarfgp`), enabling `PHI` and `THETA` to be computed from `atan2` of real parts directly.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zunbdb3 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zunbdb3';

// Build a tall and skinny complex matrix [X11; X21] with orthonormal columns. We use M=4, P=3, Q=2 (M-P=1, the zunbdb3 partition where the lower block is the smallest dimension).
const sq3 = 1.0 / Math.sqrt( 3.0 );
const sq6 = 1.0 / Math.sqrt( 6.0 );

// X11 is 3x2 (column-major), real-valued for simplicity; X21 is 1x2 (column-major). Columns of [X11; X21] are orthonormal.
const X11 = new Complex128Array([
	sq3,
	0.0,
	sq3,
	0.0,
	sq3,
	0.0,
	sq6,
	0.0,
	sq6,
	0.0,
	-2.0 * sq6,
	0.0
]);
const X21 = new Complex128Array([
	0.0,
	0.0,
	0.0,
	0.0
]);

// Output / scalar arrays
const THETA = new Float64Array( 2 );
const PHI = new Float64Array( 1 );
const TAUP1 = new Complex128Array( 3 );
const TAUP2 = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const TAUQ1 = new Complex128Array( 2 );

// Workspace of size at least max(P, M-P-1, Q-1) = max(3, 0, 1) = 3
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 4 );

zunbdb3( 'column-major', 4, 3, 2, X11, 3, X21, 1, THETA, 1, PHI, 1, TAUP1, 1, TAUP2, 1, TAUQ1, 1, WORK );

console.log( 'THETA =', Array.prototype.slice.call( THETA ) );
console.log( 'PHI   =', Array.prototype.slice.call( PHI ) );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZUNBDB3`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZUNBDB3 simultaneously bidiagonalizes the blocks of a tall and skinny matrix X with orthonormal columns:

$$
\begin{bmatrix} X_{11} \\ ----- \\ X_{21} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} P_{1} | \\ --------- \\ | P_{2} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} B_{11} \\ 0 \\ ----- \\ B_{21} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} Q_{1}^T
$$

`X11` is P-by-Q, and `X21` is (M-P)-by-Q. M-P must be no larger than P, Q, or M-Q. Routines ZUNBDB1, ZUNBDB2, and ZUNBDB4 handle cases in which M-P is not the minimum dimension.

The unitary matrices P1, P2, and Q1 are P-by-P, (M-P)-by-(M-P), and (M-Q)-by-(M-Q), respectively. They are represented implicitly by Householder vectors.

B11 and B12 are (M-P)-by-(M-P) bidiagonal matrices represented implicitly by angles `THETA`, `PHI`.

### Further Details

The upper-bidiagonal blocks B11, B21 are represented implicitly by angles `THETA(1)`, ..., `THETA(Q)` and `PHI(1)`, ..., `PHI(Q-1)`. Every entry in each bidiagonal band is a product of a sine or cosine of a `THETA` with a sine or cosine of a `PHI`. See \[1\] or ZUNCSD for details.

P1, P2, and Q1 are represented as products of elementary reflectors. See ZUNCSD2BY1 for details on generating P1, P2, and Q1 using ZUNGQR and ZUNGLQ.

### References

\[1\] Brian D. Sutton. Computing the complete CS decomposition. Numer.

Algorithms, 50(1):33-65, 2009.

</section>
